newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH CPN PETROL FIRM NEEDS $1.5 BLN IN 3 YEARS.
newsitem.headline: POLISH CPN PETROL FIRM NEEDS $1.5 BLN IN 3 YEARS.

text.p: Poland's petrol distributor CPN SA, due to be partially sold off under the government's oil sector privatisation scheme, said on Tuesday it needed $1.5 billion in investment over the next three years.
"We estimate the investment needed for modernisation...at $1.5 billion by the year 2000," CPN management board member Witold Czaja told a news conference.

The investment was needed to build about 10 new filling stations annually, increase the firm's petrol storage capacity by 50 percent to about 2.7 million tonnes and upgrade some 240 stations annually to make them environment-friendly, CPN said in a statement issued at the conference.

Under the government programme, CPN, controlling nearly 1,400 out of Poland's 4,700 petrol stations, is to become part of holding group Nafta Polska, created last year to supervise the oil sector's modernisation and privatisation.
Nafta, which has been given shares of Poland's seven refineries, is planning to sell minority stakes in them by the end of the year.

Investors in the refineries are to be given access to CPN's lucrative network as an incentive. They will also be entitled to increase their stakes in the refineries beyond 50 percent after implementing investment programmes.
CPN's financial director Jerzy Plichta said his company is forecast to net about 129 million zlotys in 1997.

In the 13 months ending in December 1996 CPN netted 133.6 million zlotys. The company decided to report results for 13 months as a separate accounting period because it was transformed into a treasury-owned joint-stock company on December 1, 1995.
During 1995's first 11 months, when CPN functioned as an enterprise directly controlled by the industry ministry, the company netted 109 million zlotys.
